headline: Council OKs two $100M sewer bond measures and up to $15M for 63rd & Prospect

sentences.text: On October 22, 2026, the council adopted Resolution 260885, which directs the City Manager to identify up to $15,000,000.00 from City funds for the 63rd & Prospect Development.
It passed Ordinance 260895 and Ordinance 260896, which each authorize sewer revenue bonds (money the city borrows) of not to exceed $100,000,000 in principal.
It passed Ordinance 260920, which authorizes spending not to exceed $1,100,000.00 on City Hall audio and video upgrades, with Willett voting Nay.

Other passed ordinances include $2,000,000.00 from the Unappropriated Fund Balance (Ordinance 260906), a one-year $1,000,000.00 cooperative agreement with Mid America Assistance Coalition (260905), and $485,424.00 moved from the Marijuana Sales Tax Fund to the Extreme Weather Program (260918).

The council also passed Ordinance 260913, which accepts a $486,054.54 grant from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, and Ordinance 260921, which appropriates $50,000.00 for a Vacant Property Education Campaign.
It adopted Resolution 260886 on Public Safety Sales Tax funding priorities as substituted, with Willett and Rogers voting Nay.
It held Committee substitute 260445, on the Country Club Plaza sidewalk right-of-way vacation, on the docket.

Several items were sent to committee, including Ordinance 260941, which would authorize taxable industrial revenue bonds not to exceed $572,500,000.00, and Ordinance 260931, which would appropriate $1,000,000.00 for a replacement playground at Barry Road Park.
